page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 8 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.se1.2xlarge exhibits modest compute capabilities. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests falls into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks (both read and write) registers in the average range, as do Passmark CPU physics and extended instruction tests. Redis SET operations and small-model LLM inference (135M) also achieve average performance tiers, whereas single-threaded compression and medium-model LLM inference (7B) perform poorly.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive CPU processing. The main tradeoff is the lower single-core execution speed and weak database operation scores, which suggest that high-throughput transactional databases may experience bottlenecks.

This instance is appropriate for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, Redis deployments, and moderate-scale web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing power. It is less appropriate for heavy compilation, complex cryptography, or large-scale machine learning inference.
